title: M/s Abdulla & Company Rice Mill v. Chief Engineer, Distribution Division & Others
coram: Arvind Kumar Tripathi, J. and Salil Kumar Rai, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed as infructuous; Clause 6.9(II)(C) challenge not decided
headnote: A rice mill challenged an Executive Engineer's order of 31.7.2012 as founded on Clause 6.9(II)(C) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, which the petitioner said had been deleted by the Fourth Amendment, 2007 dated 14.6.2008, and also sought compensation for harassment. On counsel's statement that the entire disputed amount had been adjusted in the bill, so that no further direction was required, the Division Bench dismissed the writ as infructuous. The Court did not decide whether Clause 6.9(II)(C) survived, whether the 31.7.2012 order was valid, or the claim for compensation.
facts:
M/s Abdulla & Company Rice Mill, a consumer on connection No. 150/1410/05216, petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash order dated 31.7.2012 (No. 2259) of the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division IInd, Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., Rampur, and to direct U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. to pay compensation for harassment. The mill's case was that the Executive Engineer had passed the order under Clause 6.9(II)(C) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, a provision it said had already been deleted by the Fourth Amendment, 2007 dated 14.6.2008 and published in the Gazette that day.

The writ was listed through 2012–2013 for the licensee's instructions, to trace a short counter-affidavit and a supplementary affidavit, and after one Bench recused. On 4.12.2017 counsel informed the Court that the entire disputed amount had been adjusted in the bill, so no further direction was required and the petition had become infructuous.

Prior order-sheet (17.10.2012–8.2.2013: Satya Poot Mehrotra and Het Singh Yadav, JJ., then Vineet Saran, J. with successive companion judges) is listing only — instructions, tracing affidavits, recusal, adjournments — with no interim construction. The Court did not number or construe a Code clause; the petitioner invoked Clause 6.9(II)(C) as already deleted.

principle_tags.application: The mill attacked the 31.7.2012 Executive Engineer order as passed under Clause 6.9(II)(C) after that sub-clause had, on its case, been deleted. The Division Bench did not construe Clause 6.9 or the Fourth Amendment; it dismissed the writ as infructuous once counsel said the disputed amount had been adjusted in the bill.
